d: A router that collects related messages over time and combines them into a single coherent output message.
Messaging semantics where the sender does not block waiting for the receiver to process the message before continuing.
Message delivery semantics where a message is retried until acknowledged, guaranteeing delivery but allowing possible duplicates.
Message delivery semantics where a message may be lost but is never redelivered; sender does not retry on failure.
Secondary data elements or files appended to the document message beyond its primary business payload.
A consumer that collects multiple messages over a batching window and processes them together for throughput optimization.
A standardized, technology-agnostic message schema used across the enterprise to avoid direct dependency on any system's native format.
The normalized or standardized representation of the document after transformation, serving as the canonical data format.
A connector that bridges external systems or protocols into a messaging channel, encapsulating the legacy system's API.
A connection point that joins two channel segments or a channel to an external system, enabling message flow across the boundary while preserving channel semantics.
A system management pattern that periodically clears a channel of stale or poison messages to reset system state.
The explicit binding of a message datatype to a channel at channel creation or configuration time, establishing the type contract.
The classification of datatype channels by typing rigor: static typing enforces type at compile/build time, dynamic typing enforces at message inspection time.
A decentralized integration style where each system knows only its own part of the process; there is no central orchestrator.
A resilience pattern that stops forwarding requests to a failing downstream system after a threshold of failures is exceeded.
A transformation that stores the full message body in an external store and replaces it with a lightweight reference token in the message.
operation_identifier — the name or qualified identifier of the operation being invoked on the receiver
operation_arguments — structured data representing the parameters passed to the invoked operation
command_target — the destination endpoint service or receiver on which the operation is to be executed
command_priority — urgency level that influences routing queue ordering and processor scheduling
idempotency_key — unique value the receiver uses to detect and suppress duplicate command executions
command_timeout — duration after which the sender abandons waiting for execution result
target_interface_version — version identifier enabling the receiver to select the correct operation contract
execution_context — metadata about the calling environment such as principal identity and correlation scope
result_payload — data returned by successful command execution part of request_reply exchange
fault_payload — structured error information returned when command execution fails part of request_reply
A message that encodes an invocation of an operation on the receiver, carrying method name and arguments.
A metadata field indicating the urgency or precedence level of a command message, used by schedulers and routers to order or filter command processing.
The logical or physical destination endpoint to which a command message is addressed, specifying which receiver should process the invocation.
The maximum duration a sender will wait for a command to complete before considering it failed; exceeding this triggers timeout handling or retry.
A processor that splits an incoming composite message, routes each part through separate paths, then aggregates the results.
A router that examines message payload fields to determine the destination channel, decoupling sender from destination knowledge.
A transformer that supplements an incoming message with additional data fetched from an external source before forwarding.
A transformer that removes unwanted fields from a message, reducing payload size or stripping sensitive data.
A cryptographic checksum or hash value computed over the document content to detect unauthorized alterations in transit.
The application of content_based_router to a document_message using payload fields to determine routing destination.
A unique ID placed on both request and reply messages so the sender can match responses to their originating calls.
A point-in-time capture of channel metrics (depth, oldest_message_age, error_rate) used to evaluate purge_policy conditions before triggering a purge.
A message that has caused repeated processing failures or is structurally unprocessable and blocks channel progress if retained.
The execution step that removes qualifying messages from the channel: permanent deletion, move to dead_letter_channel, or quarantine to invalid_message_channel.
An audit log recording which messages were purged, when, under which policy, and the channel_state_snapshot at purge time for replay and tuning.
A set of rules defining which messages qualify for purging: age threshold, retry exhaustion, poison detection criteria, or pattern matching on content.
The component that periodically evaluates threshold_condition and, when true, dispatches purge_action against the target channel.
A condition that initiates a channel purge cycle; may be time-based, count-based, or event-based such as threshold_exceeded.
A configurable time interval after which messages become stale_message candidates for purging; part of purge_policy definition.
A message that has exceeded its relevance window or idle duration and no longer carries actionable data for downstream consumers.
A predicate over channel_state_snapshot values that evaluates to true when purge_trigger should fire, such as depth_overflow or stale_age_exceeded.
A channel dedicated to one message type, enforcing contract clarity at the channel level rather than inside the payload.
A channel where messages go after exhausting retries, signaling a delivery failure requiring intervention.
A router that holds messages for a configurable duration before forwarding them, implementing delayed delivery semantics.
A system management pattern that reroutes messages through a debugging or inspection step before resuming normal delivery.
payload_structure: The internal data shape of a document message, comprising typed fields and nested data elements that constitute the complete business data being transmitted.
semantic_envelope: Metadata wrapper around the payload describing document provenance, intent classification, and temporal context without prescribing receiver action.
business_object_type: A typed classifier identifying the kind of business entity the document represents, such as purchase_order, invoice, or shipment_manifest.
document_schema: A formal contract defining the expected payload_structure fields, their types, cardinality, and optionality for a given business_object_type.
content_identifier: A stable unique reference (document_id, correlation token) that identifies this specific document instance across systems and message stores.
processing_hint: An optional non-directive annotation suggesting preferred handling, urgency, or routing preference without constituting a command.
document_origin: Metadata identifying the originating system, agent, or process that produced the document_message.
payload_extractor: A component that retrieves specific fields from the payload_structure for routing, correlation, or downstream transformation.
schema_registry_entry: An entry in the message_type_registry binding a business_object_type to its document_schema and authorized handlers.
The complete data content carried by a document_message, representing the full information payload without prescribing receiver action.
A component or rule set that examines document content to determine its payload type category for downstream routing.
The actual business data carried by the document message, constituting the primary payload that the receiver processes.
document_message differs from command_message by carrying data rather than prescribing method invocations.
document_message differs from event_message by carrying complete business data rather than lightweight occurrence notifications.
A transport wrapper bundling document content with its metadata, headers, and routing information for channel delivery.
The use of message_historian to archive document_message exchanges for compliance and forensic analysis.
A unique reference assigned to a document_message enabling correlation, lookup, and idempotent processing.
A unique identifier or business key that uniquely distinguishes one document instance from all others in the integration system.
A message that carries a complete data payload (e.g. a purchase order) without prescribing what the receiver must do.
document_message specializes the general concept of message, inheriting channel transport, headers, and delivery semantics.
Auxiliary descriptors attached to a document_message describing origin, timestamp, version, or business context.
A link or pointer to related documents, enabling document graphs and cross-referencing within the message stream.
The domain-specific classification of a document_message payload, distinguishing purchase orders from invoices or other business documents.
The use of message_store to persist document_message payloads enabling audit trails and replay capability.
A subscriber registration that survives broker restarts; undelivered messages are queued and delivered once the subscriber reconnects.
A router that consults a registry or lookup table at runtime to determine destinations, allowing routing rules to change without redeployment.
A correlation pattern where the final consumer sends an acknowledgment that propagates back through the routing chain to the original sender.
A reusable solution template for connecting distributed systems, codified from real-world middleware and messaging experience.
An architectural platform that combines messaging, routing, transformation, and protocol bridging into a single integration middleware layer.
A transformer that wraps or unwraps a message in an envelope to add or strip protocol-level headers for transport.
An architectural style where system components react to events published to a message bus rather than being invoked directly.
A message that notifies the receiver something has happened, typically carrying a lightweight notification payload.
The registration of a consumer's interest in receiving messages from a particular channel or topic based on content or type.
Message delivery semantics ensuring that a message is processed precisely one time, combining delivery guarantees with deduplication.
A structured record of runtime state passed alongside a command, providing the environment information needed to correctly process the operation invocation.
A data envelope containing error details returned when an operation fails, typically including fault code, description, and optional context for recovery.
Integration via shared filesystem where each system produces/consumes files, requiring conventions on naming and polling.
The assurance that a message sent over a channel will eventually be delivered, even if the receiver is temporarily unavailable.
A monitoring interface that exposes integration component status (channels healthy, queues depth, processing lag) for observability.
A unique identifier assigned to a command that allows receivers to detect and discard duplicate submissions, ensuring safe retries without double execution.
A consumer designed to safely process the same message more than once without side effects, essential for guaranteed delivery.
A coarse-grained approach to system interconnection, defined by the mechanism used to move data between systems.
A channel that captures malformed or unprocessable messages for manual inspection instead of blocking the main flow.
A system management pattern that registers interceptor objects to run before or after message processing for cross-cutting concerns.
A router that distributes messages across multiple equivalent receiver instances to spread processing load.
A discrete packet of information sent over a channel, carrying a payload and metadata for routing and processing.
An adapter linking two messaging systems or channel types so messages flow across heterogeneous middleware.
Middleware that holds a central registry of channels, routes messages between them, and manages subscriber lifecycles.
A virtual pipeline through which messages travel from sender to receiver; analogous to a typed stream or queue.
The classification or schema identifier of a message that determines which datatype channels it can traverse.
A property on a message indicating it becomes invalid after a certain time and should be discarded if not delivered.
A router that discards messages that do not meet a predicate condition, suppressing unwanted messages from downstream consumers.
A component that archives all messages passing through a channel for compliance, auditing, or forensic replay.
A component that inspects message content or metadata and forwards the message to one or more downstream channels.
A durable repository of all messages processed by an integration component, enabling replay and audit trails.
A component that modifies message structure or content as it passes through, translating between producer and consumer schemas.
A catalog that maps message type names or namespace identifiers to their schemas and handlers in the integration system.
A Façade that exposes integration functionality to internal clients while hiding the underlying messaging API and complexity.
Integration via asynchronous message passing through a message broker, decoupling sender and receiver in time and space.
Middleware infrastructure that provides channels, routing, and delivery guarantees for asynchronous message transport.
A bridge component that converts between the enterprise's canonical data model and the external system's proprietary format.
The semantic trait distinguishing document_message from command_message, indicating the receiver determines its own response.
A transformer that reconciles multiple inbound message formats into a single canonical format before routing.
The use of normalizer to reconcile incoming document_message payloads from varying formats into a canonical schema.
The parameter values supplied to the operation being invoked by a command message, structured according to the target interface's argument schema.
A named or coded reference that uniquely identifies which operation a command message is requesting, mapping to a procedure on the target system.
A centralized integration style where a single process manager directs the sequence of operations across multiple services.
The defining property of a document_message asserting the payload contains all necessary data for the consumer to act upon voluntarily.
The serialization format of the document_message payload, such as JSON, XML, YAML, or binary encoding.
The structural definition that a document_message payload conforms to, specifying fields, types, and constraints.
A classification identifier indicating the document category or business object type, enabling routing and handler selection.
The process of verifying that document content conforms to its declared payload schema before further processing.
A channel with exactly one consumer per message; guarantees that exactly one receiver processes each message.
A consumer that repeatedly queries a source for new messages rather than receiving them push-style from a channel.
A stateful component that orchestrates a multi-step business process by sending messages to channels and handling responses.
A channel where one publisher sends and all subscribed receivers consume; each gets its own copy of the message.
A router that sends the same message to a list of recipients computed at runtime from the message content or context.
Integration where one system exposes a callable API and another synchronously invokes it as if it were local.
A message exchange pattern pairing an outgoing request message with a correlated response message returned to the original sender.
A router that reorders a stream of messages into the correct sequence before passing them downstream.
A data envelope containing the return value or outcome produced by a successfully executed operation, structured to match the expected response schema.
Metadata on a reply message indicating which channel and possibly which queue the response should be routed to.
A routing pattern where each message carries its own itinerary of processing steps, executed in sequence by participating nodes.
A router that broadcasts a request to multiple recipients and then collects and consolidates all their responses.
The enforcement that a message payload conforms to its declared schema before it is routed or transformed.
The application of schema_validation to ensure document_message payloads conform to their declared payload_schema.
A routing pattern that correlates messages across multiple channels by a shared sequencing key to maintain order across streams.
Integration via a common relational schema where systems read/write shared tables as the coupling mechanism.
A component that monitors a channel and takes corrective action (e.g., resends, redirects) when abnormal conditions are detected.
A router that breaks a composite message containing multiple items into individual messages, one per item.
A recipient list with fixed destinations known at design time, compiled into the routing logic rather than derived from content.
A version descriptor indicating which contract version of the target interface a command message adheres to, enabling version-aware routing and validation.
A system management pattern that injects a known probe message into the flow to verify correct processing downstream.
A router that limits the rate at which messages pass through, protecting downstream systems from overload.
Integration that groups message production or consumption with local database updates into a single atomic unit of work.
The runtime or compile-time rule that a datatype channel accepts only messages whose datatype matches the declared type, rejecting mismatched messages.
The validation that a message's actual type matches a datatype channel's declared type at the point of send or receive.
The descriptor carried by a datatype channel identifying the exact message type, schema, or format that the channel transports.
A message consumer bound to a datatype channel that receives only messages of the declared datatype, enabling type-safe processing without runtime type checks.
A message producer bound to a datatype channel that can only publish messages of the declared datatype, preventing accidental type violations.
The linkage between a datatype channel and the formal schema or structure definition of its accepted message type.
A channel without a declared datatype that accepts messages of any type, serving as the contrast to datatype channels.
A system management pattern that taps into a channel to observe messages without disrupting the normal flow.
